ratings_why.fun: The natural Full on turn 3 gives an early spike, Tier 3-4 hands you the Moon to steer, and the capstones turn Full into a real payoff; the heavy rules load keeps it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: A public Moon you bend, plus Hares that copy other tribes' printed text, plays unlike any of today's tribes; phase cycles and text-copying exist elsewhere, so it isn't brand new.

verdict_why: Two rounds closed the real rule holes; what's left is heat for the owner to balance, and more passes would mostly make it different.

points.text: The growth shape works: a small Full spike on turn 3, steady Waxing and Waning buffs mid-game, then Moonturn multipliers and Full capstones late. Keep the four-turn rhythm; it is the tribe's identity.
Dame Waxwell reads as replacing the usual Start of Turn turn, but adding "instead of its usual turn" would make that certain.
Spring Jill is a plain 2/3 in three fights out of four. A small New or Waning line would keep it worth buying in the early turns that aren't Full.
The design's own fix (the Hare in the Moon doubles only the first Moonturn each turn) is a good fallback if the owner finds the golden almanac engine too hot. Leave it as an option, not a change.
The Three Hares on a Mad March Hare board triples every Moonturn buff across the three. That's a payoff worth climbing toward; keep it hot.

standouts.why: Changeling Sister turns placement into a puzzle: put her to the right of an off-tribe engine and Full makes a second one.
Dame Waxwell makes steering the Moon a skill test every turn: turn twice to skip a phase, or hold for another Waxing.
Mother Meikle Care is a true capstone: Full every third turn and the whole coven borrowing shapes, at the cost of Waxing.

weakest.why: Spring Jill does nothing outside Full, so it's a vanilla body most early fights.
Dew-Pond Scryer is a 2/3 whose one Moon turn matters little before Tier 3 cards exist.
Equinox Watcher's +1/+1 to other Hares is small, and holding often costs you the Moonturns you're building on.

flags.note: With Waxwell and Mad March Hare, four Moonturns give about 60 stats a turn at Tier 5, and the golden stack reaches about 270. Linear, not a loop, but far past the top of the guide.

Jill Longshanks keeps Boxing while she wins, so a big buffed copy can clear a weak board at Start of Combat and gain +2/+2 (+4/+4 at Full with the Moon-Scour) for each win. Big bodies and Bristle stop it.
The Three Hares with Mad March Hare and the Hare in the Moon multiplies the Moonturn buffs for its three units. High roll, worth the owner's eye.
